## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

On narrow layouts (iOS app), after moving a tracked expense out of the self DM via the "Submit it to someone" whisper button (select a workspace, then Create expense), the app opens the destination workspace chat — but tapping the back button there navigates to the Inbox instead of returning to the self DM the flow started from.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

When the expense confirmation step mounts on a narrow layout, it pre-mounts the destination report underneath the money-request RHP so that submitting can reveal it instantly. `IOURequestStepConfirmation` computes the destination route (the workspace chat) and hands it to the pre-mount hook:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L80-L93

That route reaches `preInsertFullscreenUnderRHP`, which dispatches the `REPLACE_FULLSCREEN_UNDER_RHP` action:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L1140-L1143

Because report routes are nested under the tab navigator, the action handler takes its tab-switch branch, and `getTargetTabRoute` rebuilds the reports tab's nested stack as just `[sidebar (Inbox), destination report]` — it deliberately prepends only the sidebar as the back target and discards everything else that was on the stack, including the self DM screen the user was actually on:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/af37ee85da464d76cc6a95a0fa9c9414dc7f2b8c/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L207-L254

When the user then presses "Create expense", the submit fast path only dismisses the RHP (the destination is already mounted underneath), so the final stack in the reports split navigator is `[Inbox, workspace chat]` — the self DM entry is gone, and back lands on the Inbox.

Without the pre-insert (for example on wide layouts), the post-submit path goes through `dismissModalWithReport`, which dismisses the RHP and then navigates to the workspace chat. That navigation is upgraded to a push, so the stack becomes `[Inbox, self DM, workspace chat]` and back correctly returns to the self DM. I confirmed both stack shapes with a navigation unit test against the current main: pre-inserting report B while report A is open yields `[Inbox, B]`, while plain post-submit navigation from report A to report B yields `[Inbox, A, B]`.

This regressed when the submit-expense flow was migrated to the pre-mount mechanism (the `usePreMountDestination` migration), which extended the Search-only pre-insert to report destinations. The same defect affects any narrow-layout confirmation flow whose destination report differs from the report currently underneath the RHP — the tracked-expense whisper flow in this issue is simply the easiest way to hit it.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `getTargetTabRoute` (with the "is the target tab already focused" information passed down from `getTabStateWithExistingFocusedTarget`), when the pre-insert target lives in the tab that is currently focused and that tab already has nested routes, we should preserve the tab's entire existing nested stack and layer the incoming destination route on top of it, instead of resetting the stack to only the sidebar plus the destination. The pre-insert eligibility check already guarantees the destination differs from the report currently on top, so no duplicate entry can be created.

Cross-tab pre-inserts (for example global-create flows that reveal the Search tab) and the workspace-navigator special case keep the current reset behavior — the change only applies to the same-tab case, which is exactly the case where the user has visible history that must survive.

With this change, the stack revealed after submitting becomes Inbox → self DM → workspace chat, so the back button returns the user to the self DM, matching what the non-pre-insert navigation path already does.

**Compare branch:** https://github.com/Expensify/App/compare/main...snorkmaiden:App:wildan/98106-preinsert-preserve-focused-tab-stack?expand=1

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Two alternatives:

1. Handle the same-focused-tab report case directly in `handleReplaceFullscreenUnderRHP` by pushing the destination report inside the existing split-navigator state rather than rebuilding the tab route's nested state. Functionally equivalent; it just moves the merge one level up.

2. Make `getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute` return no route when the destination report lives in the currently focused reports tab, so the flow falls back to the ordinary dismiss-and-navigate path (which pushes correctly). This also restores the correct back stack, but it gives up the instant-reveal performance benefit the pre-mount mechanism was built for, so correcting the merge is preferable.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

On narrow layout, the confirmation step pre-mounts the destination workspace report under the open RHP. `getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute` is narrow-gated and returns `ROUTES.REPORT_WITH_ID(destinationReportID)` when the destination report is loaded and is not already the topmost report ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L42-L92)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/getSubmitExpensePreMountDestinationRoute.ts#L42-L92)). `usePreMountDestination` then calls `Navigation.preInsertFullscreenUnderRHP`, which dispatches `REPLACE_FULLSCREEN_UNDER_RHP` ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/hooks/usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L56-L64)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/hooks/usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L56-L64), [[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L1116-L1143)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/Navigation.ts#L1116-L1143)).

Because report routes live inside `TAB_NAVIGATOR`, `handleReplaceFullscreenUnderRHP` takes the tab-target branch and rebuilds the focused Reports tab through `getTargetTabRoute` ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L416-L450)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L416-L450)). The bug is in that rebuild: for non-workspace tabs, `getTargetTabRoute` uses only `existingNestedRoutes.at(0)` as the back target, which is the Inbox/sidebar route, and never carries the currently focused Self DM report route ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L207-L237)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L207-L237)).

`[Inbox, Self DM] -> [Inbox, Workspace chat]`

The Self DM is removed before the user presses Back. Then the report pre-insert submit handler simply reveals the already-mounted destination by dismissing the RHP ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/SubmitExpenseOrchestrator.tsx#L229-L242)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/pages/iou/request/step/confirmation/SubmitExpenseOrchestrator.tsx#L229-L242), [[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/hooks/usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L70-L78)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/hooks/usePreMountDestination/index.ts#L70-L78)), leaving Inbox as the only back destination.

`[Inbox, Self DM, Workspace chat]`

Use route identity, not just route name, when deduping. For report routes, that means comparing `name` plus `params.reportID`, because both Self DM and workspace chat have the same screen name.

The cancel path should not need special handling because the original tab route is already saved before pre-insert and restored by `handleRemoveFullscreenUnderRHP` ([[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L453-L460)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L453-L460), [[source](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L519-L529)](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/c3f72ff6790c5e7d68ed6eb8970f3ec7d09e0dcc/src/libs/Navigation/AppNavigator/createRootStackNavigator/GetStateForActionHandlers.ts#L519-L529)).

Add focused unit coverage in `handleReplaceFullscreenUnderRHP` tests for:

1. `[Inbox, Report(A)] + pre-insert Report(B) -> [Inbox, Report(A), Report(B)]`.
2. Re-dispatching the same destination does not duplicate `Report(B)`.
3. Existing `WORKSPACE_NAVIGATOR` seeding behavior remains unchanged.

Skipping report pre-insert for this flow would avoid the bad stack, but it removes the instant reveal optimization and leaves the shared navigation reducer broken for other report pre-inserts.

Passing a `backTo` route to the workspace report would mask this one header-back case, but `backTo` is legacy/deprecated in the navigation guide, and it would not fix the underlying stack loss or native/system back behavior.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

**Paid report still listed under Approved (the real bug)**

Spend → Reports uses search type `expense-report` ([`SearchUIUtils.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1025e4d222abda31cb7e49b50e50fd5d8d93dda7/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L777-L781)). [`getSections`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1025e4d222abda31cb7e49b50e50fd5d8d93dda7/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L3749-L3764) routes that type into `getReportSections`.

Inside `getReportSections`, client-side status filtering only runs when the query type is `expense`:

```ts

const shouldShow =

!isActionLoading && currentQueryJSON?.type === CONST.SEARCH.DATA_TYPES.EXPENSE

? isEligibleForStatus(currentQueryJSON, reportItem)

: true;

```

([`SearchUIUtils.ts` ~2948](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/1025e4d222abda31cb7e49b50e50fd5d8d93dda7/src/libs/SearchUIUtils.ts#L2947-L2948))

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The break is in how a new expense picks the report to join — not in any approval gate. When User B creates the new expense from the workspace chat, `getMoneyRequestInformation` resolves the reuse candidate from exactly one place, `chatReport.iouReportID`, and never looks anywhere else:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/61544d3ed27b6f986eb6b212d700eb1d3b8d73d9/src/libs/actions/IOU/MoneyRequestBuilder.ts#L1356-L1371

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/61544d3ed27b6f986eb6b212d700eb1d3b8d73d9/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L11548-L11568

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/61544d3ed27b6f986eb6b212d700eb1d3b8d73d9/src/libs/actions/IOU/ReportWorkflow.ts#L1404-L1416

It is not the held report. This is why the bug is specific to the submitter and a solo repro wouldn't show it.

Here's the part that rules out the approval-gate theories other proposals lean on: the held report is genuinely addable. https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/61544d3ed27b6f986eb6b212d700eb1d3b8d73d9/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L2941-L2963

# Proposal
## Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.
After a workspace enables **Rules** and upgrades, the Workspace Settings > Rules page shows "Billable default" as **Non-billable**, but the Billable toggle does not appear on the expense confirmation page. The toggle only starts appearing after the admin opens Rules > Billable default and explicitly saves a value — and crucially they cannot simply re-save "Non-billable", they have to switch to **Billable → Save → back to Non-billable → Save**. So there are two defects: the Rules page mislabels the state, and the only way out of that state is a two-save workaround.
## What is the root cause of that problem?
Billable tracking on a policy is controlled by **two separate fields**:
- `policy.defaultBillable` — the billable/non-billable *value*.
- `policy.disabledFields.defaultBillable` — whether billable tracking is **enabled at all**. When this is `true`, billable is fully disabled and the field is hidden everywhere it's consumed.

Every new workspace is created with billable tracking turned off by default, regardless of whether Rules is later enabled:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L2582-L2585

`enablePolicyRules()`, which runs on Step 4-5 ("Enable Rules" / "Upgrade workspace"), only merges `areRulesEnabled` and the max-expense-value fields — it never touches `disabledFields.defaultBillable`, so it stays `true` (disabled) after Rules is turned on:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L5349-L5431

The confirmation page correctly hides the Billable toggle in this state. `shouldShowBillable` is derived from `isBillableEnabledOnPolicy(policy)`:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/components/MoneyRequestConfirmationListFooter/hooks/useFooterDerivedFlags.ts#L96

which explicitly checks `disabledFields?.defaultBillable !== true`, so it returns `false` while tracking is disabled:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/libs/MoneyRequestReportUtils.ts#L28-L30

### Defect 1 — the Rules list page mislabels the disabled state
The classic (non-Rules-Revamp) "Individual expense rules" section computes the summary text purely from `policy?.defaultBillable`, ignoring `disabledFields.defaultBillable` entirely:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/pages/workspace/rules/IndividualExpenseRulesSection.tsx#L114

Since `defaultBillable` defaults to `false`, this row always renders "Non-billable" — even though billable tracking is actually off — falsely implying the setting is live. That's exactly what the tester sees in Step 6.

This inconsistency was already fixed once in the newer Rules-Revamp variant of the same section, which correctly gates the text on tracking being enabled and renders an empty string (shown muted) otherwise:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/pages/workspace/rules/IndividualExpenseRulesSectionRevamp.tsx#L96-L97

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/pages/workspace/rules/RulesBillableDefaultPage.tsx#L48-L50

and gates Save on it:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/pages/workspace/rules/RulesBillableDefaultPage.tsx#L80

Saving *anything* is what fixes it, because `setPolicyBillableMode` unconditionally clears the disabled flag as a side effect of any save:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/libs/actions/Policy/Policy.ts#L6576-L6586

So the state transition the user needs (`disabledFields.defaultBillable: true → false`) is a real, savable change that `hasChanges` simply doesn't count.

Original:
https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ae20d461051eca40fb30cb4cc9c08a72106db7e6/src/pages/workspace/rules/IndividualExpenseRulesSection.tsx#L114

```ts
const billableModeText = isBillableEnabledOnPolicy(policy) ? translate(`workspace.rules.individualExpenseRules.${policy?.defaultBillable ? 'billable' : 'nonBillable'}`) : '';
```

This requires adding `isBillableEnabledOnPolicy` to the existing import of `MoneyRequestReportUtils` at the top of the file (it's a plain pure function, no new hook/Onyx connection needed). The empty string is rendered as a muted title by the existing `individualExpenseRulesItems` list, consistent with every other "unset" row in that list (e.g. `maxExpenseAmountText`/`reimbursableModeText`).

**2. Count "tracking is currently disabled" as a pending change** so the setting can be enabled in a single save:

```ts
const isBillableTrackingDisabled = policy?.disabledFields?.defaultBillable === true;
const hasChanges = selectedBillable !== persistedBillable || isBillableTrackingDisabled;
```

This is accurate rather than a workaround: when tracking is disabled, saving genuinely changes the policy (`setPolicyBillableMode` flips `disabledFields.defaultBillable` to `false`), so Save should not be disabled. ## Proposal

### Please re-state the problem that we are trying to solve in this issue.

After a partial approval (the approver approves only the un-held expense), the held expense is split into its own still-open report. When the submitter then creates a new expense from that same workspace chat, the expense lands in a brand-new report instead of joining the report that holds the on-hold expense.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

When a new expense is created from a policy expense chat, App resolves the report to reuse **solely** from `chatReport.iouReportID` — [`getMoneyRequestInformation`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/actions/IOU/MoneyRequestBuilder.ts#L1358-L1365):

```ts
} else if (!allReports?.[`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.REPORT}${chatReport.iouReportID}`]?.errorFields?.createChat) {
    iouReport = allReports?.[`${ONYXKEYS.COLLECTION.REPORT}${chatReport.iouReportID}`] ?? null;
}
```

Whether that report is reused or a new one is created is then decided by [`shouldCreateNewMoneyRequestReport`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L11548-L11568) → [`canAddTransaction`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L2941-L2963) → [`canAddOrDeleteTransactions`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L2912-L2931). An **approved** report fails that gate, so `shouldCreateNewMoneyRequestReport` returns `true`.

The gap is that a partial approval produces **two** reports on the same chat:

- the report that was approved (the un-held expense), and
- a separate report that still holds the on-hold expense — which is `PROCESSING`/awaiting first-level approval and _would_ pass `canAddTransaction`.

App optimistically repoints `chatReport.iouReportID` to the held report during the approve flow — [Hold.ts:801-825](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/actions/IOU/Hold.ts#L801-L825) — but that code only runs on the **approver's** client. The submitter never runs it; on the submitter's client `chatReport.iouReportID` resolves to the just-**approved** report. Because `canAddTransaction(approvedReport)` is `false`, `shouldCreateNewMoneyRequestReport` returns `true` and a new report is spawned, even though a perfectly addable held report already exists on the very same chat.

In short: the reuse logic looks at exactly one report (`chatReport.iouReportID`) and, when that one is not addable, immediately creates a new report instead of checking whether another still-open report on the same chat can accept the transaction.

<details>
<summary>Evidence (from the attached video, submitter's client)</summary>

The chat (`.../r/8207575970829155`) shows the approved report (`d1`, "Approved") and, separately, the held expense (`d2`, "This expense was put on hold"). Creating `d3` from this chat produces a **new** "Expense Report … · Draft · 1 expense" instead of adding `d3` to the held report — confirming the reuse target resolved to a non-addable report and no addable sibling was considered.

</details>

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In [`getMoneyRequestInformation`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d313529253bcca95d8dafa60db976254afefd09b/src/libs/actions/IOU/MoneyRequestBuilder.ts#L1356-L1382) STEP 2, when the report referenced by `chatReport.iouReportID` is missing or **not** addable (and no explicit report was requested), fall back to the submitter's newest outstanding report on the policy — the same source the confirmation page's Report field already uses ([`getOutstandingReportsForUser`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d313529253bcca95d8dafa60db976254afefd09b/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12041-L12058)) — before building a brand-new report:

```ts
if (isPolicyExpenseChat && !existingIOUReport && !moneyRequestReportID && (!iouReport || !canAddTransaction(iouReport))) {
    const outstandingReport = getOutstandingReportsForUser(chatReport.policyID, payeeAccountID)
        .filter((report): report is OnyxTypes.Report => !!report && canAddTransaction(report))
        // `created` is an ISO timestamp, so a lexicographic compare keeps the newest report first.
        .sort((reportA, reportB) => ((reportB.created ?? '') < (reportA.created ?? '') ? -1 : 1))
        .at(0);
    if (outstandingReport) {
        iouReport = outstandingReport;
    }
}
```

With `iouReport` now pointing at the held (addable) report, `shouldCreateNewMoneyRequestReport` returns `false` and the new expense is added to it — matching the expected result. This covers every creation flow (manual, scan, distance, per diem) since they all pass through this function.

The confirmation page has the mirror-image gap — [`ReportField`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d313529253bcca95d8dafa60db976254afefd09b/src/components/MoneyRequestConfirmationList/sections/ReportField.tsx#L84-L89) trusts `iouReportIDFromMain` without checking it is outstanding — so apply the same check there, so the report shown on the confirmation page matches where the expense actually lands:

```ts
const isIOUReportFromMainOutstanding = !!iouReport && isReportOutstanding(iouReport, policyID, reportNameValuePairs, false);
const outstandingReportID = isPolicyExpenseChat ? ((isIOUReportFromMainOutstanding ? iouReportIDFromMain : undefined) ?? availableOutstandingReports.at(0)?.reportID) : reportID;
```

I verified this fix on a test branch: https://github.com/snorkmaiden/App/tree/test/98017-hold-partial-approve-reuse-report

### What specific scenarios should we cover in automated tests to prevent this from happening again in the future?

I added these in [`GetMoneyRequestInformationTest.ts`](https://github.com/snorkmaiden/App/blob/d313529253bcca95d8dafa60db976254afefd09b/tests/actions/IOU/GetMoneyRequestInformationTest.ts):

- Given a policy expense chat whose `iouReportID` points to an **approved** (non-addable) report, and a separate `PROCESSING`/awaiting-first-level report owned by the submitter on the same policy: creating a new expense resolves `iouReport` to the addable outstanding report, not a new one.
- Given only a non-addable report and no outstanding sibling: a new report is still created (no regression to normal behavior).

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

Repoint `chatReport.iouReportID` to the held report for **all** clients on partial approval (i.e. mirror the optimistic [Hold.ts:801-825](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/bc3e21cdc99a22fce235bcbd47b246af23a559c4/src/libs/actions/IOU/Hold.ts#L801-L825) repoint on the backend so the submitter also receives it). This addresses the pointer at its source, but it lives in `Auth`/`Web-Expensify` and needs an internal engineer; the App-side fallback above fixes the user-facing behavior on every client regardless of which report `iouReportID` ends up on.
